title: Gradebook with weighted categories
prompt:
Build a gradebook in Python as a package grades/ with grades/__init__.py, grades/book.py and grades/export.py.
- grades/book.py: letter(percent) -> "A" (90 and up), "B" (80 and up), "C" (70 and up), "D" (60 and up) or "F". class Gradebook(weights) where weights is {category: percent}; the percents must add up to 100, otherwise ValueError. add_score(student, category, score, out_of): an unknown category or out_of <= 0 or a score outside 0..out_of raises ValueError. average(student) -> the weighted average percent rounded to 2 decimals: each category's percent is (sum of scores / sum of out_of * 100), and categories with no scores for that student are left out with the remaining weights scaled up to 100; a student with no scores raises KeyError. students() -> the names sorted. ranking() -> a list of (student, average) sorted by average, highest first (ties by name).
- grades/export.py: to_csv(book, path) writes the header student,average,letter then one row per student in sorted order, with the average written with 2 decimals (e.g. 87.50).
Write unit tests too.
